title: Frontend architecture and fidelity
summary: Operational rules for diagnosing computed CSS, keeping a change in the right cascade layer, matching the real runtime, previewing before production, and letting utilities serve tokens. Each rule links the CSS Snapshot 2026 section or module for that subject.

rules.title: Fix source of visual defects
rules.intent: Read the computed value and the cascade step that produced it before adding !important
principles: Inspect the computed value with getComputedStyle before editing the stylesheet
A declaration wins by origin and importance, then cascade layer, then specificity and order. Name the step that is already winning
!important raises a declaration and reverses layer order: for important rules, the earlier layer wins. It is not a diagnosis
acceptance: Before and after, plus the cascade step that caused the defect, are recorded
limitations: Cascade 5 is a reliable Candidate Recommendation in CSS Snapshot 2026. The official definition still lists Cascade 4, which Cascade 5 extends
CSSOM, which defines getComputedStyle, is grouped with modules of rough interoperability

rules.title: Minimize affected scope
rules.intent: Keep a local correction inside the component's layer so it does not interleave with the rest of the origin
principles: Put a local fix in that component's rule or cascade layer. Layers keep one concern from interleaving with rules outside the layer
An unlayered author rule joins an implicit final layer, so a document-wide patch beats layered component styles for normal declarations
Use containment when the subtree's layout must be processed independently of the rest of the page
antiPatterns: Broad global rule for local defect
acceptance: Shared consumers of a changed layer or shared rule are rechecked
limitations: Cascade layers are in the snapshot's reliable Candidate Recommendations, not yet in the official definition
CSS Nesting is listed with rough interoperability. It can group a component's rules, and it is not a stability guarantee
Containment isolates rendering. It does not choose which cascade layer wins

rules.title: Match target runtime
rules.intent: Preview in the project's CSS engine, because an unsupported value drops the whole declaration and a pre-CR feature is not stable CSS
principles: CSS Snapshot 2026 defines CSS by module stability, not by what one browser has shipped
A renderer with no support for a value must ignore the entire declaration, not the unsupported piece. A different pipeline will not show that fallback
Treat a feature as unstable until its spec is a Candidate Recommendation, unless the snapshot lists it as safe to release. Branch on real support with @supports
Use the project framework, CSS pipeline, providers, and fonts in the preview
antiPatterns: Vanilla recreation claimed as exact component
acceptance: Runtime parity limitations are disclosed, including any pre-CR feature in use
limitations: Section 3 of the snapshot is written for implementers. The author-facing rule, that a partial environment is not the product, is derived from those requirements

rules.title: Isolated workspace
rules.intent: Try an unproven visual change in a controlled preview so production content does not depend on it
principles: The snapshot allows unstable CSS in a limited, controlled environment and warns against content that depends on it in production
Review the preview, then integrate a patch. The first look does not land in the live stylesheet
antiPatterns: Editing live production app for first preview
limitations: The spec's controlled environment is about shipping unstable CSS, not about a code sandbox. Using a sandbox to satisfy that warning is operational guidance

rules.title: Utility CSS with design intent
rules.intent: Let utility classes resolve to shared custom properties, which are the CSS mechanism for a value defined once
principles: A custom property holds a value in one place and propagates it. Utilities implement those tokens
Define the product's values in the theme the project already uses, such as Tailwind's theme, instead of a one-off utility that hardcodes a look
Judge the result visually. The utility syntax is not the design
acceptance: Repeated colors, type, and spacing trace back to a custom property or the project theme
limitations: Tailwind is not part of CSS Snapshot 2026. Custom properties are the platform primitive. The theme page is the library's own documentation

rules.title: Preserve behavior
rules.intent: Change presentation without changing the document's semantics or the control's behavior
principles: CSS describes presentation and usually does not change the semantics of the document language. A visual fix keeps the element that already has the behavior
The appearance property switches how a native control is drawn. The control remains that control
Keyboard operation, accessible name, and application logic stay intact after the visual change
antiPatterns: Replacing functional inputs with static look-alikes
acceptance: The same actions still run after the visual change
limitations: The snapshot states the semantics boundary. It does not list every HTML control. Component behavior stays in the HTML and ARIA specs
